heading: Dummy node unlocks uniform swapping
body:
A **dummy node** pointing to the head gives every node a predecessor. Without it, swapping the first pair requires special-case logic (no node before head). With it, you rewire pointers the same way for all pairs:
- `prev.next = second`
- `first.next = second.next`
- `second.next = first`

heading: Three-pointer dance
body:
Track **`prev`**, **`first`**, **`second`** to swap adjacent pairs:
1. `prev.next = second` — skip over `first`
2. `first.next = second.next` — connect `first` to rest
3. `second.next = first` — complete the swap

Then move `prev = first` to prepare for the next pair. Loop while two nodes remain.

label: Core Swap · Python
code:
def swapPairs(head):
    dummy = ListNode(0)
    dummy.next = head
    prev = dummy
    
    while prev.next and prev.next.next:
        first = prev.next
        second = first.next
        
        prev.next = second
        first.next = second.next
        second.next = first
        
        prev = first
    
    return dummy.next

q: Why is a dummy node essential for this problem?
options: It provides a predecessor for the head node, allowing uniform swap logic without special-casing the first pair
It reduces the time complexity from O(n²) to O(n)
It prevents infinite loops when the list has an odd number of nodes
It stores the original head for later reference
explain: The dummy node gives the head a predecessor, so swapping the first pair uses the same three-step pointer rewiring as all other pairs.
